reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real normed inner-product space of dimension n+1, where n is any natural number, and let A:E→E be a continuous real linear symmetric operator. Give the unit sphere S={x∈E:‖x‖=1} its n-dimensional sphere manifold structure, and define f:S→ℝ by f(y)=⟨y,Ay⟩. Let Df(x) be the manifold derivative used by the Lean statement, totalized to zero outside differentiability. For every x∈S, both of the following equivalences hold: Df(x) is the zero linear map if and only if Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x; and Df(x) is the zero linear map if and only if there exists a real scalar μ such that Ax=μx and x≠0. Thus the zero-differential condition at the chosen unit vector is equivalent to that vector being an eigenvector, with its eigenvalue given by the quadratic value ⟨x,Ax⟩.
